proof_audit.judgment: Strictly increasing concave utility on a common wage interval; inverse-convexity proof, all-action affine IC/IR, mixed-action averaging, supported global multiplier certificate. Existence and strict uniqueness are conditional, not presumed; weak recommendation/participation ties stated.

Independent global IR/floor lower bounds and exact attaining wages for all B>=0. Complete optimal wage face when B>=1, strict-selection infimum and separate H/L/no-contract comparison. Risk-neutral transfer cancellation is not applied to later risk-averse cases.

Exact quadratic remainder and nonnegative multipliers certify unique global wages; full-information Jensen insurance and target thresholds independently reconstructed. Both effort utilities tie, so wage uniqueness does not imply strict effort.

Positive action laws justify both likelihood-ratio/conditional-law directions. Common fiber conditioning preserves every action utility and common wage bounds, and Jensen weakly reduces bills. Strict ancillary-risk loss and the original strict four-state gain are distinct claims; extra state constraints/fees require new checks.

Completed squares prove a stationary minimum versus a changed maximum. All positive, zero and negative spreads covered to rule out every interior target in the original technology. Concavity is only a stated sufficient condition for worker global choice under a given contract.

Full finite recursion has exact promise equality, every current action comparison, date-specific continuation participation and terminal infeasibility. Conditioning and stitching prove both directions. Global behavioral/private-history worker optimality follows by finite induction under no private saving or persistent state. Deterministic wage/pure public-target class, compact wage boxes and finitely many target/deviation trees prove attainment. No public-lottery or infinite-horizon existence claim.

Branchwise completed-square minimization, explicit monotonicity and convexity, unconstrained smoothing and later-exit reoptimization. Initial IR is slack at b=3/4; H/L/no-contract comparisons include actual dated costs. An optional cap4 embeds the same optima in the bounded recursion without asserting that the uncapped domain is compact.

Game action rights, public output/payments and hidden effort are explicit. Worker global current IC, every firm payment choice and both public states checked. Private history is irrelevant to future primitive laws, so finite backward replacement works at each private information history; a uniform bounded discounted tail proves full behavioral best replies. Continuous payment histories are handled pointwise rather than called finite. Patience threshold is confined to the salary/bonus/fallback class; unilateral credibility is not renegotiation proof.

limits: Synthetic laws identify model implications, not empirical contract effects or current legal rights.
Common wage bounds and full-support finite signal laws delimit the sufficiency result; stricter statewise constraints may block conditioning.
Finite promise theorem excludes public randomized recommendations/contracts, private credit, persistent hidden state and unmodeled history-dependent rights.
Relational theorem is a fixed zero-salary nonnegative success-bonus game with a specified public fallback, not universal stationarity, minmax, renegotiation-proof or private-monitoring contracting.
Three quiet runtime gates establish reproducibility and bindings, not mathematical completeness by themselves. Root and separate peer/dependency acceptance remain outside author completion.
